newsitem.title: UK: McDonald's shares off on Big Mac attack talk.
newsitem.headline: McDonald's shares off on Big Mac attack talk.

text.p: Shares in McDonald's Corp were down $3/8 at $47 in European trade on Wednesday following press reports that the company planned to begin its biggest discounting programme to date.

Company Vice Chairman Jack Greenberg will pitch the move, which will include cutting the price of a big Mac from $1.90 to $0.55 with the purchase of fries and a drink, to franchisees tomorrow, the Wall Street Journal said.
"We've seen some erratic trade in McDonald's this morning," one market maker said. "We saw some initial buying but then sellers emerged."
The shares in the fast-food giant touched a morning high of $47-3/4, up $3/8 on the New York close before news spread of the possible price cutting plans.
"There is talk around the market that it costs a McDonald's franchisee $0.62 to make a Big Mac. A price war could hurt them in the short-term," another dealer said.
The report cited an internal document that said "McDonald's pricing isn't competitive" and that price cuts could turn around "the declining momentum of sales, transaction and cash flow."
A majority of franchisees in each market must support the plan for it to be approved, the paper said, adding that Greenberg has been lobbying franchisees for support in recent days.
